Primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs retention and format, encryption at rest with KMS/HSM, and data residency/retention policies. Action items agreed to deliver SOC2 and integration docs, schedule pricing/pilot follow-up.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 14:00 PT | Duration: 55 mins
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Martin Kline (Zenith), Aisha Byrne (Zenith), Liam O'Connor (Zenith), Sana Park (Zenith Legal)

00:00 Ethan Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate the time. quick intro, I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood. Priya is our solutions engineer. can you go around on your side?
00:12 Martin Kline: Yeah, Martin Kline, head of cloud security at Zenith. we're evaluating vendors for inference, interested in redwood for low-latency routing and also posture.
00:20 Aisha Byrne: Aisha here, VP Eng, mostly concerned about integration surface and data retention.
00:25 Liam O'Connor: Liam, platform, will be owner on our side for infra and network.
:35 Sana Park: Sana from legal, I'll jump in on DPA and contract questions.

01:05 Priya Nair: Thanks, Martin. quick agenda: SOC 2 / ISO evidence, SSO and RBAC, audit logs & retention, encryption and KMS, and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). sound right?
01:12 Martin: yes, that covers it. top priority is that we can meet our compliance controls.

03:02 Ethan: To start, we are SOC 2 Type II, our report covers the controls for our hosted service. we also have an ISO 27001 gap analysis underway, not fully certified for iso yet. the SOC 2 report is available for review under NDA.
03:20 Martin: ok, do you have SOC 2 last audit date?
03:24 Ethan: last audit period ended 2025-12-31, report issued 2026-01. we'll send the redacted report.
03:34 Martin: good. are there any scope exclusions for Hosted? like do logs or keys ever leave a customer-specific boundary?
03:45 Priya: for Hosted, logs live in our managed environment; we retain audit events by default 90 days, longer retention is available as an add-on. keys for customer data at rest are in our KMS — for hosted customers we manage keys, but we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via customer KMS for Dedicated/Private options.
04:10 Martin: okay BYOK is important. do you support HSM-backed keys?
04:14 Priya: yes we integrate with cloud KMS and support HSM-backed keys where the cloud provider exposes that capability; for Private we can support on-prem HSMs in many cases.

06:00 Aisha: for SSO, we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. we also want role sync from our idp to maintain least privilege.
06:12 Priya: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and our RBAC model maps to groups and roles. there are a few default roles and you can create custom roles. small caveat, some legacy fields in our UI are labeled differently in the transcripts so mapping might need a quick mapping table — sorry poor wording in docs sometimes.
06:35 Martin: can SCIM de-provision and what about stale accounts audit?
06:40 Priya: SCIM supports create/update/deactivate flows. de-provisioning timing depends on your IdP and SCIM sync interval but typically immediate. audit logs include user lifecycle events with timestamps, which you can export to S3 or stream to your SIEM.

09:20 Liam: network constraints — for Dedicated we want VPC peering or private link — how do you handle egress and inbound?
09:30 Ethan: Dedicated supports customer VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalents; Private (VPC/offline) gives you customer-controlled networking. Hosted uses our managed endpoints over TLS. For strict network isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
09:50 Liam: latency is also a factor; how big a perf delta with Private on-prem vs Hosted?
09:56 Priya: it varies — Private on-prem will be fastest if co-located with your infra; Hosted is optimized for multi-tenant low-latency but Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation. we can run benchmarks during PoC.

12:05 Martin: audit logs format — do you have schema? we need immutable logs for certain controls.
12:12 Priya: yes logs are JSON lines with standardized fields: timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id. note: the transcript may mislabel some fields, but logs are structured. we support append-only storage and can configure retention policies and export streams to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules.
12:40 Martin: can logs be forwarded to our SIEM in near real-time?
12:44 Priya: yes we support streaming to syslog/CloudWatch/EventHub and we also provide a Kafka export for enterprise setups. latency for streaming is sub-60s typically.

15:10 Martin: encryption at rest — is all customer data encrypted?
15:14 Priya: yes at rest and in transit TLS 1.2+/1.3. for Hosted we manage keys by default; BYOK supported for Dedicated/Private, and customer-managed KMS keys can be used for S3 and disk encryption.
15:30 Martin: do you support envelope encryption?
15:33 Priya: yes we use envelope encryption patterns and can integrate with your KMS for wrapping keys.

18:00 Aisha: retention policy question — we have regulatory requirement for 7 years for certain logs. you said 90 days default, how costly is longer?
18:12 Ethan: longer retention is an add-on; cost depends on volume. we can give a pricing table. in Dedicated/Private you can apply your own S3 lifecycle which helps reduce cost.

22:05 Sana Park: from legal side, we need DPA with standard EU data processing addendum and data residency statements. do you have EU region options?
22:15 Ethan: yes we have EU-hosted regions. Private deployments can be fully in-custody. we do offer data residency guarantees for enterprise contracts.
22:30 Sana: also need breach notification timelines and subprocessor list.
22:35 Ethan: we'll send our subprocessor list and security playbook, and we have standard 72-hour breach notification clause.

25:50 Martin: about ISO 27001 — you said gap analysis, any timeline to certification?
25:55 Priya: we aim for certification in H2 2026, currently remediating one control set. SOC 2 Type II is our primary artifact today.

29:30 Liam: for pilot, we want to test model hosting with real PII redaction workflows, can we run in Dedicated or Private?
29:40 Priya: yes pilot can run on Dedicated reserved capacity with network peering. we can run a short-lived Private pilot if required for strict compliance, but that does add setup time.

33:10 Martin: are there support SLAs for incident response?
33:15 Ethan: enterprise tiers include 24x7 on-call and defined response times; we'll include SLA details in the follow-up.

36:00 Aisha: one more — RBAC granularity, can we restrict model access by team and environment, and can we limit token generation rates per role?
36:12 Priya: yes roles can be scoped by project and environment; rate limits and quotas can be applied to tokens or routes. we also have route-level auditing.

39:40 Martin: any third-party pen tests or attestations?
39:45 Ethan: we do annual pen tests and engage a 3rd-party assessor; summary reports are available under NDA.

42:00 Sana: on contracts — can you accommodate standard customer security addendum?
42:06 Ethan: yes we typically negotiate addenda; we'll share our standard security exhibit.

47:10 Recap: Priya: Action items — we'll send SOC 2, SSO guide, RBAC doc, and pilot scoping template. Ethan will send subprocessor list and pricing for retention add-on. Zenith to confirm data retention requirements and legal contact.

48:05 Martin: timeline — we'd like a pilot in next 4 weeks, decision by end of Q2 if pilot good.
48:12 Ethan: sounds good, we'll target follow-up week of 2026-03-23 to review pilot scope and Dedicated pricing.

52:00 Aisha: thanks everyone, helpful session.
52:05 Priya: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the pricing call.
52:12 Ethan: thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes: occasional transcription errors, speaker overlaps and some proper nouns mis-transcribed. references to docs: SOC2 report (link sent under NDA), SSO integration guide (link), RBAC best-practices doc (link), pilot scoping template (link).
